findings.title: float: right on .small-action button is silently ignored inside the new flex container
findings.body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flex container via `@include flexbox()`. CSS specifies that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` on the direct-child `button` (line 309) no longer does anything. Previously the button was pinned to the right edge of the small-action row; now it will render inline immediately after `.small-action-desc`, breaking the intended layout of small action posts (e.g. the edit/expand controls). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 271), which is harmless only by accident of source order. The fix is to replace the button's float with `margin-left: auto` (or add `flex` spacing) so it is pushed to the end of the flex row.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align, which does not support the 'baseline' value used by bullet badges
findings.body: The new `align-items` mixin unconditionally emits `-webkit-box-align: $alignment` for the 2009 flexbox spec, but that old property only accepts start/end/center/stretch — `baseline` is invalid and the declaration is dropped. `.badge-wrapper.bullet` in badges.css.scss calls `@include align-items(baseline)`, so on browsers that only understand the old `-webkit-box` model (e.g. older iOS Safari, which Discourse's `display: -webkit-inline-box` fallback in `inline-flex()` explicitly targets) the invalid declaration is ignored and items fall back to stretch alignment, vertically misaligning the bullet color swatch against the category text. If old-WebKit support matters (the mixin's prefixes imply it does), the mixin needs a value mapping or a fallback for `baseline`.

findings.title: Header panel alignment now depends entirely on flexbox with no fallback for non-flex browsers
findings.body: `.panel` previously used `float: right`, which worked in any browser. It now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the `.contents` flex container. In any browser where none of the `display` values emitted by the `flexbox()` mixin are supported, `.contents` stays a block container, an auto left margin on a block-level `.panel` computes to 0, and the panel (user menu, search, hamburger icons) collapses against the logo on the left instead of staying on the right, breaking the header layout. If the supported-browser matrix includes any non-flexbox browsers (or engines with buggy partial flex support such as IE10, where auto margins inside `-ms-flexbox` containers are unreliable), this needs a fallback such as retaining `float: right` alongside the flex rules.
